''[[Grey's Anatomy]]'' is an American [[medical drama]] [[television series]] that premiered on the [[American Broadcasting Company]] (ABC) as a [[mid-season replacement]] on March 27, 2005.<ref name="NYT">{{#invoke:cite|news|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9A04E2DA133EF937A25757C0A9639C8B63|title=Thriving Ratings for a New Patient on ABC|last=Rhodes|first=Joe|date=April 14, 2005|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=July 1, 2009|archive-date=November 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121107211442/http://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9A04E2DA133EF937A25757C0A9639C8B63|url-status=live}}</ref> The series focuses on the fictional lives of [[surgery|surgical]] [[internship (medicine)|interns]] and [[residency (medicine)|residents]] as they evolve into seasoned doctors while trying to maintain personal lives. The show's premise originated with [[Shonda Rhimes]], who serves as an executive producer, along with [[Betsy Beers]], [[Mark Gordon (film)|Mark Gordon]], [[Krista Vernoff]], [[Rob Corn]], [[Mark Wilding]], and [[Allan Heinberg]].<ref name="ATS">{{#invoke:cite|web|title=About the Show|url=http://abc.go.com/shows/greys-anatomy/about-the-show|work=[[Grey's Anatomy]]|publisher=[[American Broadcasting Company]]|access-date=May 26, 2012|archive-date=June 15, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120615183950/http://abc.go.com/shows/greys-anatomy/about-the-show|url-status=live}}</ref> The series was created to be racially diverse, utilizing a [[colour-blind casting|color-blind casting]] technique.<ref name="CBCT">{{#invoke:cite|news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/05/08/arts/television/08foge.html?pagewanted=print|title='Grey's Anatomy' Goes Colorblind|newspaper=The New York Times|date=May 8, 2005|first=Matthew|last=Fogel|access-date=June 27, 2012|archive-date=April 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150421172230/http://www.nytimes.com/2005/05/08/arts/television/08foge.html?pagewanted=print|url-status=live}}</ref> It is primarily filmed in [[Los Angeles]].<ref>{{cite video|year=2005|title=Grey's Anatomy Season One DVD: Commentary Feature|publisher=[[Walt Disney Studios Home Entertainment|Buena Vista Home Entertainment]]}}</ref> The show's title is a play on ''[[Gray's Anatomy]]'', the classic [[human anatomy]] [[textbook]].

Episodes have been broadcast on Thursday nights since [[Grey's Anatomy season 3|''Grey's'' third season]].<ref>{{#invoke:cite|web| url=https://www.today.com/popculture/can-greys-rise-challenge-thursdays-wbna14893769 | title=Can 'Grey's' rise to challenge of Thursdays? | work=[[Today (American TV program)|Today]] | date=September 24, 2006 | access-date=August 4, 2012 | author=Berman, Craig | archive-date=July 29, 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200729090301/https://www.today.com/popculture/can-greys-rise-challenge-thursdays-wbna14893769 | url-status=live }}</ref> The first two seasons aired after ''[[Desperate Housewives]]'' in the Sunday 10:00 pm EST time-slot.<ref name="NYT"/> All episodes are approximately forty-three minutes, excluding commercials, and are broadcast in both [[high-definition television|high-definition]] and [[standard-definition television|standard]].<ref name=AHDN>{{cite episode|title=[[A Hard Day's Night (Grey's Anatomy)|A Hard Day's Night]]|credits=Writer: Rhimes, Shonda. Director: Horton, Peter|series=Grey's Anatomy|network=American Broadcasting Company|airdate=March 27, 2005|season=1|number=1}}</ref> Episodes are also available for download at the [[iTunes Store]] in standard and high definition,<ref name=ITHSD>{{#invoke:cite|web|title=Grey's Anatomy, Season 8|url=https://itunes.apple.com/us/tv-season/greys-anatomy-season-8/id460131426|work=[[iTunes]]|date=March 26, 2005 |access-date=May 27, 2012|archive-date=September 15, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180915164939/https://itunes.apple.com/us/tv-season/greys-anatomy-season-8/id460131426|url-status=live}}</ref> and [[Amazon Prime Video]],<ref name=AIV>{{#invoke:cite|web|title=Grey's Anatomy Season 7, Ep. 3 'Superfreak'|url=https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0046FA6EU|work=[[Amazon Prime Video]]|access-date=May 27, 2012|archive-date=February 11, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170211160644/https://www.amazon.com/dp/B0046FA6EU|url-status=live}}</ref> with new episodes appearing the day after their live airings. ABC [[Video on demand]] also releases episodes of the show, typically one to two days after their premieres.<ref name="on demand">{{#invoke:cite|web| url=http://adage.com/article/media/watch-grey-s-anatomy-skip-ads/125354/ | title=Watch 'Grey's Anatomy' When You Want, Just Don't Skip Ads | work=[[Advertising Age]] | date=February 26, 2008 | access-date=June 29, 2012 | author=Steinberg, Brian | archive-date=January 10, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160110185033/http://adage.com/article/media/watch-grey-s-anatomy-skip-ads/125354/ | url-status=live }}</ref> Recent episodes are available on ABC's Android/iTunes app or at ABC's official ''Grey's Anatomy'' website, and [[Hulu]].<ref name=GAVFE>{{#invoke:cite|web|title=Grey's Anatomy Video and Full Episodes|url=http://abc.go.com/shows/greys-anatomy/video|work=Grey's Anatomy|publisher=American Broadcasting Company|access-date=May 27, 2012|archive-date=February 13, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120213173236/http://abc.go.com/shows/greys-anatomy/video|url-status=live}}</ref>

''Grey's Anatomy'' was among the ten highest-rated shows in the United States from the [[Grey's Anatomy season 1|show's first]] through [[Grey's Anatomy season 4|fourth season]]. The show's episodes have won a number of [[List of awards and nominations received by Grey's Anatomy|awards]], including a [[Golden Globe Award for Best Television Series – Drama|Golden Globe Award for Best Drama Series]],<ref name=ATS/> a [[People's Choice Award]] for Favourite TV Drama,<ref name=seriespplchoice>{{#invoke:cite|web|title=People's Choice Awards Nominees and Winners: 2007|url=http://www.peopleschoice.com/pca/awards/nominees/index.jsp?year=2007|work=People's Choice Awards|publisher=Procter & Gamble|access-date=May 23, 2012|archive-date=April 28, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120428091745/http://www.peopleschoice.com/pca/awards/nominees/index.jsp?year=2007|url-status=live}}</ref> and multiple [[NAACP Image Award for Outstanding Drama Series|NAACP Image Awards for Outstanding Drama Series]].<ref name="odsn">{{#invoke:cite|web|url=http://www.naacpimageawards.net/42/winners-and-honorees/television/ |title=The 42nd NAACP Image Awards&nbsp;– Television |publisher=[[National Association for the Advancement of Colored People]] |work=[[NAACP Image Award]]s |access-date=June 29, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120625093121/http://www.naacpimageawards.net/42/winners-and-honorees/television/ |archive-date=June 25, 2012 }}</ref> Since its premiere, [[Walt Disney Studios Home Entertainment|Buena Vista Home Entertainment]] has distributed all seasons on DVD. There have been several special episodes recapping events from previous episodes, and two series of webisodes.

In 2010, ABC signed a deal allowing ''Grey's Anatomy'' episodes to be streamed on [[Netflix]], and in 2024, all episodes became available on [[Hulu]].<ref name=GANFX>{{cite magazine|last=McMillan|first=Graeme|title=Netflix Adds More ABC, Disney Shows For Instant Streaming|url=https://techland.time.com/2010/12/08/netflix-adds-more-abc-disney-shows-for-instant-streaming/|magazine=[[Time (magazine)|Time]]|access-date=May 27, 2012|date=December 8, 2010|archive-date=April 15, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120415131853/http://techland.time.com/2010/12/08/netflix-adds-more-abc-disney-shows-for-instant-streaming/|url-status=live}}</ref> In April 2018, ''Grey's Anatomy'' became the [[List of programs broadcast by the American Broadcasting Company|longest-running drama ever for ABC]], and the [[List of longest-running American primetime television series|longest-running American primetime medical drama ]] after the network renewed the series for a fifteenth season, surpassing [[ER (TV series)|''ER'']] (1994–2009).<ref>{{#invoke:cite|news|url=https://variety.com/2018/tv/news/greys-anatomy-renewed-season-15-abc-1202777808/|title='Grey's Anatomy' Renewed for Season 15 at ABC|last=Otterson|first=Joe|date=April 20, 2018|website=Variety|access-date=April 21, 2018|language=en-US|archive-date=April 12, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200412071232/https://variety.com/2018/tv/news/greys-anatomy-renewed-season-15-abc-1202777808/|url-status=live}}</ref> On March 30, 2026, [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]] renewed the series for a twenty-third season.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Andreeva |first=Nellie | date=March 30, 2026 |title=‘Grey’s Anatomy’ Renewed For Season 23 By ABC As 2 Longtime Cast Members Depart|url=https://deadline.com/2026/03/greys-anatomy-renewed-season-23-abc-cast-return-status-1236769222/|access-date=March 30, 2026 |website=[[Deadline Hollywood]] |language=en-US}}</ref>

* [[Kate Walsh (actress)|Kate Walsh]] ([[Addison Montgomery|Dr. Addison Montgomery]]) joins the cast after guest starring in the Season 1 finale, "[[Who's Zoomin' Who? (Grey's Anatomy)|Who's Zoomin' Who?]]".
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 2}}

=== Season 3 (2006–07) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 3|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 3}}
* [[Sara Ramirez]] ([[Dr. Callie Torres]]) & [[Eric Dane]] ([[Mark Sloan (Grey's Anatomy)|Dr. Mark Sloan]]) joined the main cast.
* [[Isaiah Washington]] ([[Preston Burke|Dr. Preston Burke]]) and [[Kate Walsh (actress)|Kate Walsh]] ([[Addison Montgomery|Dr. Addison Montgomery]]) departed the series after the season finale, "[[Didn't We Almost Have It All? (Grey's Anatomy)|Didn't We Almost Have It All? ]]". Walsh would later star in the spin-off series ''[[Private Practice (TV series)|Private Practice]]'' and return for guest appearances in subsequent seasons, while Washington only returned to guest star in the season 10 episode, "[[We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together (Grey's Anatomy)|We Are Never Ever Getting Back Together]]". 
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 3}}
<!-- To edit the episodes in this section, you need to edit the article listed above. -->

=== Season 4 (2007–08) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 4|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 4}}
* [[Chyler Leigh]] ([[Lexie Grey|Dr. Lexie Grey]]) joined the main cast after previously guest starring on the final 2 episodes of [[Grey's Anatomy season 3|Season 3]].
* Touchstone Television was replaced by ABC Studios after the second episode, "[[Love/Addiction]]".
* After guest starring in several episodes from Seasons 2 & 3, [[Brooke Smith (actress)|Brooke Smith]] ([[Erica Hahn|Dr. Erica Hahn]]) was promoted to the main cast starting from episode 5 "[[Haunt You Every Day]]".
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 4}}
<!-- To edit the episodes in this section, you need to edit the article listed above. -->

=== Season 5 (2008–09) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 5|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 5}}
* [[Kevin McKidd]] ([[Dr. Owen Hunt]]) and [[Jessica Capshaw]] ([[Arizona Robbins|Dr. Arizona Robbins]]) joined the cast. 
* [[Brooke Smith (actress)|Brooke Smith]] ([[Erica Hahn|Dr. Erica Hahn]]) departed the series after the seventh episode, "[[Rise Up (Grey's Anatomy)|Rise Up]]".
* [[T.R. Knight]] ([[Dr. George O'Malley]]) departed the series after the season finale, "[[Now or Never (Grey's Anatomy)|Now or Never]]". His character was mentioned and appeared through archival footage in subsequent seasons, while Knight eventually returned to guest star in the Season 17 episode, "[[You'll Never Walk Alone (Grey's Anatomy)|You'll Never Walk Alone]]".
* The series reached 100 episodes with the season's 22nd episode, "[[What a Difference a Day Makes (Grey's Anatomy)|What a Difference a Day Makes]]"
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 5}}

* [[Kim Raver]] ([[Teddy Altman|Dr. Teddy Altman]]) joined the main cast starting from episode 19 "[[Suicide Is Painless (Grey's Anatomy)|Suicide is Painless]]".

Raver would eventually re-join the main cast  in [[Grey's Anatomy season 15|Season 15]], while Leigh only returned to guest star in the Season 17 episode, "[[Breathe (Grey's Anatomy)|Breathe]]".

* [[Patrick Dempsey]] ([[Dr. Derek Shepherd]]) departed the series after the season finale, "[[You're My Home (Grey's Anatomy)|You're My Home]]", Dempsey eventually returned to guest star several episodes in [[Grey's Anatomy season 17|Season 17]].
* [[Caterina Scorsone]] ([[Amelia Shepherd|Dr. Amelia Shepherd]]), [[Kelly McCreary]] ([[Maggie Pierce|Dr. Maggie Pierce]]) and [[Giacomo Gianniotti]] ([[Andrew DeLuca|Dr. Andrew DeLuca]]) joined the cast, Scorsone had previously portrayed the character on the spin-off ''[[Private Practice (TV series)|Private Practice]]''.

* [[Sara Ramirez]] ([[Dr. Callie Torres]]) departed the series after the season finale, "[[Family Affair (Grey's Anatomy)|Family Affair]]".

=== Season 14 (2017–18) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 14|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 14}}
* [[Jake Borelli]] ([[Levi Schmitt|Dr. Levi Schmitt]]) joined the cast.
* [[Martin Henderson]] ([[Nathan Riggs|Dr. Nathan Riggs]]) departed the series after the fifth episode, "[[Danger Zone (Grey's Anatomy)|Danger Zone]]".
* [[Jessica Capshaw]] ([[Arizona Robbins|Dr. Arizona Robbins]]), [[Sarah Drew]] ([[April Kepner|Dr. April Kepner]]) and [[Jason George]] (Dr. Ben Warren) departed the series after the season finale, "[[All of Me (Grey's Anatomy)|All of Me]]". George would later star on the spin-off series, ''[[Station 19]]'', while Drew and Capshaw would eventually returned to the series for several guest star appearances in Seasons [[Look Up Child (Grey's Anatomy)|17]], [[You Are the Blood|18]] and [[Baby Can I Hold You (Grey's Anatomy)|20]], respectively.
* The series reached 300 episodes with the season's seventh episode, "[[Who Lives, Who Dies, Who Tells Your Story (Grey's Anatomy)|Who Lives, Who Dies, Who Tells Your Story]]"
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 14}}
<!-- To edit the episodes in this section, you need to edit the article listed above. -->

=== Season 15 (2018–19) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 15|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 15}}
* [[Kim Raver]] ([[Dr. Teddy Altman]]) was promoted to the main cast, marking her first series-regular appearance since the Season 8 finale, "[[Flight (Grey's Anatomy)|Flight]]".
* [[Greg Germann]] ([[Tom Koracick|Dr. Tom Koracick]]) joined the cast.
* The Mark Gordon Company was replaced by Entertainment One after the tenth episode, "[[Help, I'm Alive (Grey's Anatomy)|Help, I'm Alive]]".
* The series surpassed [[ER (TV series)|ER]] as the [[List of longest-running American primetime television series|longest-running American primetime medical drama series]] with the season's fifteenth episode and 332nd episode overall, "[[We Didn't Start the Fire (Grey's Anatomy)|We Didn't Start the Fire]]".
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 15}}
<!-- To edit the episodes in this section, you need to edit the article listed above. -->

=== Season 16 (2019–20) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 16|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 16}}
* [[Justin Chambers]] ([[Dr. Alex Karev]]) departed the series after the sixteenth episode, "[[Leave a Light On (Grey's Anatomy)|Leave a Light On]]".
* ABC Studios was replaced by ABC Signature after the season finale, "[[Put on a Happy Face]]".
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 16}}
<!-- To edit the episodes in this section, you need to edit the article listed above. -->

=== Season 17 (2020–21) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 17|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 17}}
* [[Giacomo Gianniotti]] ([[Andrew DeLuca|Dr. Andrew DeLuca]]) departed the series after episode nine, "[[In My Life (Grey's Anatomy)|In My Life]]".
* [[Jesse Williams (actor)|Jesse Williams]] ([[Jackson Avery|Dr. Jackson Avery]]) and [[Greg Germann]] ([[Tom Koracick|Dr. Tom Koracick]]) both departed the series after the season finale, "[[Someone Saved My Life Tonight (Grey's Anatomy)|Someone Saved My Life Tonight]]". Both actors kept making recurring appearances in subsequent seasons, with Williams returning most frequently.
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 17}}

=== Season 18 (2021–22) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 18|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 18}}
* The series reached 400 episodes with the season's twentieth episode and season finale, "[[You Are the Blood]]".
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 18}}
<!-- To edit the episodes in this section, you need to edit the article listed above. -->
=== Season 19 (2022–23) ===
{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 19|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 19}}
* [[Alexis Floyd]] (Dr. Simone Griffith), [[Harry Shum, Jr.]] (Dr. Benson "Blue" Kwan), [[Adelaide Kane]] (Dr. Jules Millin), [[Midori Francis]] (Dr. Mika Yasuda), and [[Niko Terho]] (Dr. Lucas Adams) all joined the cast.
* [[Kelly McCreary]] ([[Maggie Pierce|Dr. Maggie Pierce]]) departed the series and Entertainment One was replaced by Lionsgate Television after the season finale, "[[Grey's Anatomy season 19#ep420|Happily Ever After?]]", due to Lionsgate's acquisition of eOne.
* [[Ellen Pompeo]] ([[Meredith Grey|Dr. Meredith Grey]]) scaled back her role in the series starting from this season. Pompeo will appear in a limited quantity of episodes per season, while retaining her roles as an executive producer and narrator of the series.
{{:Grey's Anatomy season 19}}

{{main|Grey's Anatomy season 21|label1=''Grey's Anatomy'' season 21}}
* [[Jake Borelli]] ([[Levi Schmitt|Dr. Levi Schmitt]]) and [[Midori Francis]] (Dr. Mika Yusuda) left the series by episode 7 and 8, respectively. Borelli is credited as a series regular for episode 17, "[[Love You Like a Love Song (Grey's Anatomy)|Love You Like a Love Song]]". 
* [[Jason George]] (Dr. Ben Warren) joined as a series regular again once the spin-off ''[[Station 19]]'' concluded.

=== ''Seattle Grace: Message of Hope'' ===
{{#invoke:Episode table|main |anchor=Message of Hope|background=#FF5F64 |overall=5 |title=28 |director=14 |writer=25 |airdate=25 |dontclose = y}}
{{#invoke:Episode list|sublist|Seattle Grace: Message of Hope
 |EpisodeNumber= 1
 |Title= No Comment
 |DirectedBy= Kevin McKidd
 |WrittenBy= Chris Van Dusen
 |OriginalAirDate= {{Start date|2010|10|14}}
 |ShortSummary= Richard has a meeting with a P.R. firm, to help with him get people to come back to the hospital, since people don't find it safe to go to the hospital. She makes him watch the interview he gave to someone, and it shows that he avoids the subject. She wants to start a sizzle reel, showing that the hospital is back, and better than ever. When April comes in to get the chief, he asks what she thought, she avoids the subject basically saying it was bad. The P.R. firm representative then tries to convince him into it.
 |LineColor= FF5F64
}}
{{#invoke:Episode list|sublist|Seattle Grace: Message of Hope
 |EpisodeNumber= 2
 |Title= Take One
 |DirectedBy= Kevin McKidd
 |WrittenBy= Chris Van Dusen
 |OriginalAirDate= {{Start date|2010|10|21}}
 |ShortSummary= Owen is the first one of the staff to be part of the 'sizzle reel'. During the taping of his commercial, he insist that parts of his speech sounds wrong. When she asks him to make it sound like he isn't reading, he says to move the card away, and when she does so he can't read the card. Karen then says that they need a younger, and more energetic person to do the sizzle reel, and that just isn't what Dr. Hunt is. Chief then has to let Owen go in order to find a new spokesperson.
 |LineColor= FF5F64
}}
{{#invoke:Episode list|sublist|Seattle Grace: Message of Hope
 |EpisodeNumber= 3
 |Title= The Face
 |DirectedBy= David Greenspan
 |WrittenBy= Chris Van Dusen
 |OriginalAirDate= {{Start date|2010|10|28}}
 |ShortSummary= When April starts to take her role at the 'sizzle reel' Karen insist that Jackson would be the better face for the role. April gets offended at this, and says that now she has nothing to do. Karen says that she would rather have someone who looks like Jackson operate on her, than April. Chief then has to fire April from the camp again to help the hospital.
 |LineColor= FF5F64
}}
{{#invoke:Episode list|sublist|Seattle Grace: Message of Hope
 |EpisodeNumber= 4
 |Title= Nerves
 |DirectedBy= David Greenspan
 |WrittenBy= Miguel Nolla
 |OriginalAirDate= {{Start date|2010|11|4}}
 |ShortSummary= Avery continues to practice his part for the commercial. Karen then starts unbutton Avery's shirt a little, and says that it shows that women are the ones that are in need of this sizzler. When Avery actually gets on camera to shoot the sizzler, he begins to laugh nonstop from nervousness. Avery says that he's had this since he was a child, and Karen says that he should've said it at the beginning. After Avery leaves Karen says that they should put Richard on camera because he'll be the best for it.
 |LineColor= FF5F64
}}
{{#invoke:Episode list|sublist|Seattle Grace: Message of Hope
 |EpisodeNumber= 5
 |Title= Award-Winning
 |DirectedBy= Kevin McKidd
 |WrittenBy= Chris Van Dusen
 |OriginalAirDate= {{Start date|2010|11|11}}
 |ShortSummary= While Richard is practicing Karen tells him that he should be himself, but without glasses. When Richard is taping the 'sizzler', Karen stops the taping to put awards in front of the camera to add more effect. When Karen tries to show a patient that's just be released from the OR Richard shoots this down, and says that it would not happen. Richard then says that the 'sizzle reel' isn't going to work. He says that none of this is real, and he would not actually say anything from the script. She then says that he needs to 'pitch instead of bitch' and tell her what he wants to say.
 |LineColor= FF5F64
}}
{{#invoke:Episode list|sublist|Seattle Grace: Message of Hope
 |EpisodeNumber= 6
 |Title= The Sizzle
 |DirectedBy= Kevin McKidd
 |WrittenBy= Tim Day
 |OriginalAirDate= {{Start date|2010|11|18}}
 |ShortSummary= The 'sizzler' that was taped airs and show interviews of all the doctors that went through the shooting, and they each say that they are only stronger since the shooting has happened. They also each explain what made them doctors and why they love their jobs. After Richard and Karen view the commercial she says that it was the most honest commercial that she's made, and that she loves it.
 |LineColor= FF5F64
}}
{{End|html=y|Episode table}}
